chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) and asked him about the man who emancipates a young boy, or an elderly old man, or one afflicted with a chronic illness, or one who has no means of livelihood.

So he (peace be upon him) said: Whoever emancipates an owned slave who has no means of livelihood, it is obligatory upon him (the emancipator) to support him (the freed slave) until he becomes self-sufficient. And similarly did Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to do when he emancipated the young and those with no means of livelihood.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin — title of Imam 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.حِيلَةَ: means, recourse, or ability to earn a livelihood
key_terms.زَمَانَةٌ: chronic illness or permanent disability that prevents self-sufficiency
key_terms.مَمْلُوكاً: an owned slave, one under complete legal ownership
key_terms.يَسْتَغْنِيَ: to become self-sufficient, no longer in need of another's support
key_terms.يَعُولَهُ: to support, maintain, or provide financial sustenance for someone

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on supporting a freed slave who is young, elderly, or chronically ill and cannot support themselves?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal responsum from Imam al-Ridha (AS) to Ibn Mahboub regarding the obligations that arise when a person frees a helpless slave — whether young, elderly, or chronically ill. The Imam rules that the emancipator bears the financial responsibility to support the freed slave until that person can sustain themselves independently. The ruling is reinforced by citing Imam 'Ali (AS) as a precedent, grounding the jurisprudential verdict in the practice of the Commander of the Faithful.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> and asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who emancipated a young boy, or an old Sheykh, one with chronic illness, and the one for whom there is no dodge for him.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who emancipates an owned slave for whom there is no means (of earning) for him, so upon him is that he shelters him until he is self-sufficient from him, and similar to that is what Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> did, when he<sup>asws</sup> emancipated the young and the one for whom there is no means (of earning)’.
